item.text: The workload identity module has two self-contained utility classes with direct tests. I’m reading their test coverage and call sites next; this will show whether there’s room for a real cleanup without changing public behavior.

This area is narrow enough to refactor safely. The main structural issue I see is that `SizeLimitInputStream` uses an atomic counter even though `InputStream` reads are not made thread-safe here, which makes the implementation noisier and suggests a guarantee it doesn’t provide.

I found the same size-limiting stream pattern in workload identity, inference, and watcher. The implementations diverge in small but important ways: two count requested bytes rather than actual bytes read, and one can count EOF attempts. I’m going to normalize the structure around “record successful bytes read” and add focused regression coverage.

I’m editing the three `SizeLimitInputStream` implementations plus their unit tests. The code change is deliberately small: count only bytes that were actually returned by the wrapped stream and keep the limit check in one helper.
The refactor is in place. I’m checking the relevant Gradle project paths and then I’ll run the smallest test tasks that cover the touched classes.
